demographics.trauma_type: Accidentally caused serious injury to another

Triggers.value: Physical pain in a part of the body

Threat.value: I am unable to relax even when I know I am in a safe place
I feel threatened by strangers approaching me even in ordinary situations
I watch other people closely for signs that they might harm me

Memory.value: When memories come to mind of what happened, I feel my body is in the same position as when the frightening event occurred.
When I remember the event I feel intense rage
When I remember the event I feel overwhelming grief

Negative Appraisals.value: There is something about me that made the event happen
I am no longer capable of doing the things that defined me

vignette: As a forester, Ryan had spent his career navigating the dense woods of the Pacific Northwest. But it was on one fateful day, three years ago, that his life took a devastating turn. While operating a chainsaw, he lost control and severely injured a young colleague, Alex. The sound of the saw, the scent of freshly cut wood, and the sight of blood-soaked flannel would forever be etched in Ryan's mind. In the aftermath of the accident, Ryan found himself constantly on edge. Physical pain in his hands, reminiscent of the day he lost control of the chainsaw, would send him spiraling into a state of hypervigilance. He couldn't relax even when he knew he was in a safe place, always watching others closely for signs that they might harm him. Strangers approaching him, even in ordinary situations, made him feel threatened. Proximity to the forest, where the accident occurred, filled him with an overwhelming sense of dread. As memories of that day flooded his mind, Ryan would often find himself reenacting the physical sensations he experienced during the accident - his body tensed up, as if still gripping the chainsaw. The recollections were accompanied by intense rage and grief, emotions that left him breathless and exhausted. When these memories arose, they inevitably triggered more pain in his hands, creating a self-reinforcing cycle. The more Ryan dwelled on these memories, the more he began to question his own reliability. He couldn't shake the feeling that there was something inherently flawed about him that had led to the accident. His self-doubt grew, and with it, an increasing sense of inadequacy - he no longer felt capable of doing the job that had defined him for so long. As Ryan's negative appraisals deepened, they began to influence his perceptions of the world around him. He started to view strangers as potential threats, which in turn made him more vigilant and reactive. This cycle further eroded his sense of self-trust, making it even harder for him to navigate everyday situations. In recent months, Ryan's struggles had taken a toll on his marriage and work life. His wife, Sarah, grew increasingly concerned about his withdrawal from social interactions and his obsessive focus on the accident. At work, Ryan found himself struggling to complete tasks that once came naturally to him. The anxiety and self-doubt had become too much to bear. It was this accumulation of distress, coupled with a growing realization that he couldn't continue living in such a state, that finally brought Ryan to seek help. He hoped that therapy might offer a way out of the darkness that had consumed him since that fateful day in the forest - a way to break free from the cycle of pain, fear, and self-doubt that had become his constant companion.
